title: I Forwarded the Stealth Fee to Every Name on the Wedding Invoice

parts.text: I opened the final wedding invoice and found a line named energy. Six hundred dollars. I am twenty-seven, dental-receptionist organized. Our photographer, Jules, had been sweet for months. The contract, initialed, had a cap on extras. Energy was not in it. My partner Malik was tasting cake crumbs off a paper plate. The plate was from the grocery bakery, because we are not fancy. Jules emailed that energy meant overtime vibes, not hours. Jules said, "It's standard to collect energy after long days" I said, "Standard is the PDF we signed" The reception ended at 9:02. The contract overtime started at 10. I highlighted 9:02 in the timeline she herself sent. My aunt had paid a deposit as a gift. I felt sick involving her. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. parts.text: I cc'd every name on the original contract, including Jules's studio bookkeeper. The bookkeeper, Ron, asked Jules to show the clause. There was no clause. The energy line vanished in a revised PDF within an hour. Jules sent a hurt paragraph about artists and respect. I replied with page four, overtime, 10 p.m. Malik ate the rest of the grocery cake. We still used the photos. They are good. Good photos are not a vibe tax. Ron added a checkbox to their template after that, which I know because he emailed thanks. Ron said, "Where is energy in the addenda" Jules said, "I'll remove it" My aunt never had to know the almost-fight. I told her anyway, because gifts deserve honesty. She laughed and said energy should have been coffee. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there. I remember the cheap smell of the room, which is how I know I was there.
